tiktok.titulo:
Where does fat actually go when you burn it?
You don’t sweat it out — you literally breathe it out.
The real science of fat loss in 20 seconds.
#FatLoss #FitnessTips #WeightLossScience #HealthFacts
Your body actually changes in your twenties and it can take a bit longer for the numbers to shift, but stay consistent with your goals! #motivation #fyp

facebook.texto: "Ozempic gave me my health back, but left me with skin that looked like deflated balloons. This locker room selfie? Proof that loose skin isn't permanent. If you're one of the millions who've transformed with GLP-1 medications, you know this story. The number on the scale drops dramatically. Your health markers improve. But then... the skin. I lost 65 pounds in 8 months. Incredible for my health, challenging for my confidence. The rapid weight loss left me with loose, crepey skin that made me fe

analise_criativa.avatar: Woman in a locker room taking a mirror selfie in a bikini, appearing to be in her 40s-50s, showcasing a toned/transformed body after weight loss
analise_criativa.editing: Static image split layout — Facebook ad library screenshot showing the creative on the right. Image is a candid-style locker room selfie, natural lighting, no heavy editing. Feels authentic and personal.
analise_criativa.observation: The ad is technically about loose skin after Ozempic/GLP-1 use, not a direct weight loss supplement pitch. The brand page '40 Plus & Fabulous' and the destination domain 'besque.co' suggest a body oil or skin tightening product. The copy hooks on a very specific pain point (loose skin post-GLP-1) which is a growing niche. Page profile image shows illustrated curvy women in lingerie which contrasts with the photorealistic ad image.
analise_criativa.highlight: Strong emotional hook targeting a very specific and underserved audience — Ozempic/GLP-1 users with loose skin. The locker room selfie feels raw and relatable. The '65 pounds in 8 months' specificity adds credibility. Copy angle of 'deflated balloon skin' is visceral and scroll-stopping. Worth testing against body transformation audiences and GLP-1 keyword traffic.

facebook.texto: Lost 60 pounds on Ozempic. My reward is legs I'm still too ashamed to show anyone. No shorts. No sundresses. No pool days with my grandkids. My dermatologist told me there wasn't much I could do about it. Turns out my collagen cells weren't dead. They were starved and asleep. Okay. I want to tell you exactly who that dermatologist was and exactly what she said, because if you've heard the same words from your own doctor, I think you need to read this carefully. I'm 56. I lost 60 pounds on Ozempi

analise_criativa.avatar: Woman in her mid-50s in a locker room, wearing a dark bikini, standing confidently — appears to be a before/after style reveal. Profile picture shows an older woman in a pink blazer suggesting the persona 'Nora Davies' is a real or semi-real character.
analise_criativa.editing: Static image ad. Locker room setting with natural overhead lighting. Candid, unpolished aesthetic consistent with UGC style. Image feels personal and diary-like rather than produced.
analise_criativa.observation: Same copy and same avatar name 'Nora Davies' as Ad 3 — this appears to be an A/B test with different creative images. Both launched the same date (Jun 27, 2026) and have been active 28 days. Destination domain is 'offer.trynurovita.com' suggesting a supplement or topical skin product. The ad is framed as a personal story but functions as a lead gen hook to a VSL.
analise_criativa.highlight: The specific shame-based copy ('legs I'm still too ashamed to show anyone', 'no pool days with my grandkids') is emotionally powerful and highly relatable for the 50+ female demographic. The dermatologist authority reversal ('collagen cells weren't dead, they were starved and asleep') creates strong curiosity. Locker room image adds authenticity. High potential for the GLP-1 adjacent audience.

analise_criativa.editing: Static image, natural outdoor lighting, appears to be a poolside or patio environment. Slightly more relaxed and lifestyle-oriented than the locker room image in Ad 2. Still candid and unproduced.
analise_criativa.observation: Identical copy to Ad 2 — confirmed A/B split test on image only. Ad 3 uses an outdoor/poolside image while Ad 2 uses a locker room image. Both running simultaneously since Jun 27, 2026 under the same 'Nora Davies' page. The outdoor image may resonate differently with the copy line 'no pool days with my grandkids' creating stronger visual-copy alignment.

Worth tracking which image wins this split test. The combination of shame, specific age (56), specific weight loss amount (60 lbs), and authority betrayal (dermatologist) makes this a well-constructed DR hook.

facebook.texto: The problem wasn’t fat… it was trapped water! My GP looked at me and said: “It’s just menopause, love. You’ll have to get used to it.” My jaw hit the floor. I was 52, sitting in a cramped NHS office. I had waited three weeks for a 10-minute appointment, and in less than 60 seconds, he dismissed two years of my misery with a single sentence. Get used to what, exactly? Get used to the 22 lbs (over 1.5 stone) I’d piled on since menopause without changing a single thing in my diet? Get used to my st

analise_criativa.avatar: Woman aged ~52, relatable plus-size avatar visible in profile photo, ad image shows close-up of swollen/puffy feet and ankles resting on a surface — visceral body symptom visual tied to menopause weight and water retention
analise_criativa.editing: Static image, raw and unpolished feel, no graphic design overlay. Feet photo is unfiltered and deliberately unglamorous to build authenticity and emotional identification
analise_criativa.observation: The page name 'Mary Scott' presents as a personal account rather than a brand, reinforcing the UGC/testimonial disguise. The copy is exceptionally strong — NHS dismissal narrative, menopause framing, trapped water reframe. Keyword is 'salt trick' which aligns with the water retention angle. Running only on Facebook.
analise_criativa.highlight: Extremely strong story-driven hook with emotional resonance for UK women 45-60. The 'trapped water not fat' reframe is a powerful pattern interrupt. NHS frustration narrative will resonate deeply with British audience. Feet/ankle swelling image is scroll-stopping and emotionally charged. High testing priority.

I found a reason to get up. To turn the light off. To look away. And th

analise_criativa.avatar: Woman in her 40s with blonde hair, wearing a purple/lavender athletic top, photographed outdoors in a natural setting. Appears fit and confident, likely positioned as an after or aspirational figure. Couple context implied by ad copy.
analise_criativa.editing: Static image ad with overlaid text banner at top right reading 'Oze... availa...' suggesting Ozempic alternative branding. Clean lifestyle photography with natural lighting. Text-heavy copy in feed with emotional narrative hook.
analise_criativa.observation: The ad copy is unusually long and emotionally narrative — structured like a personal confession or diary entry around a 20th anniversary. This is a sophisticated advertorial-style hook designed to trigger deep emotional resonance around body image shame and intimacy avoidance. The image partially shows what appears to be a product or branding element (Oze...) which skirts the product visibility filter but the main subject is a real person.
analise_criativa.highlight: Exceptionally strong emotional copywriting angle — using relationship intimacy and self-worth as the pain point rather than typical weight loss framing. The anniversary narrative with withdrawal behavior is a powerful scroll-stopper for women 35-55. High curiosity gap created before any solution is mentioned. Worth testing this emotional hook angle with a clean talking head video format.

The couple image adds a relational dimension that directly mirrors the anniversary story in the copy, creating stronger visual-copy alignment. analise_criativa.editing: Static image of older couple with same overlaid branding banner as Ads 2 and 3. Warm natural lighting, candid photography style. Identical copy to Ads 2 and 3 — third image variant in the same split test.
analise_criativa.observation: Third creative variant of the same campaign using an older couple image. This variant targets a slightly older demographic segment (late 50s-60s) with the same anniversary/intimacy copy. The progression across Ads 2, 3 and 5 shows a deliberate age-demographic targeting strategy: solo younger woman → middle-aged couple → older couple, all with identical copy.
analise_criativa.highlight: The older couple variant is strategically interesting for the UK market where the 50-65 female demographic has high purchasing power and strong emotional resonance with long-marriage anniversary themes. If the copy is performing, this age-matched image variant could show strongest CTR with older segments. The three-variant age-demographic testing strategy is sophisticated and worth replicating.

facebook.texto: This is why your skin turned loose and deflated after GLP-1 weight loss, and it has nothing to do with "not losing weight fast enough." If you've lost 40, 60, 80 pounds on Ozempic, Wegovy, or Mounjaro... if your arms hang loosely and look deflated even though you're at a healthy weight... if your chest, neck, and stomach have that soft, saggy texture you weren't expecting... You've probably been told "just give it time" or "your skin will eventually retract on its own." Maybe you've waited month

analise_criativa.avatar: Woman in casual/beach setting — Frame 1 shows a person's legs and hand pinching loose skin near the knee area on what appears to be a beach. Frame 2 shows a blonde woman wrapped in a towel holding what appears to be a small bottle. Frame 3 shows a close-up of a toned arm/body area suggesting skin improvement.
analise_criativa.editing: Vertical short-form video style typical of TikTok/Reels UGC. Low impression count badge visible. Raw, authentic handheld aesthetic. Close-up body shots designed to show skin texture before and after. Subtitles present throughout.
analise_criativa.observation: Frame 2 shows the woman holding a small bottle/product which could be a borderline product reveal, however it is not clearly branded or identifiable. The creative targets a very specific post-GLP-1 weight loss sub-niche — loose skin after Ozempic/Wegovy/Mounjaro use. This is a sophisticated angle targeting people already on or post GLP-1 drugs. Running in Germany (DE) with English copy is unusual and may indicate broad targeting or translation oversight.
analise_criativa.highlight: The post-GLP-1 loose skin angle is a high-opportunity emerging niche with very low competition. Targets an audience who has already spent money on weight loss solutions and has a new specific pain point. The pinching loose skin gesture in frame 1 is a powerful visual hook that is visceral and immediately relatable to the target demographic.
